title: Weigh Your Own Words: Improving Hate Speech Counter Narrative Generation via Attention Regularization
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the effectiveness of new attention regularization techniques (EAR and KLAR) in improving a Large Language Model's ability to automatically generate specific, suitable, and diverse counter narratives in response to hate speech. In terms of religion, it specifically measured how well the model generated open-ended counter speech against anti-Muslim and anti-Jewish hate speech.
findings: The paper found that standard fine-tuning of GPT-2 often caused the model to overfit to identity terms (like 'Muslim' or 'Jew'), resulting in generic or vague counter narratives. By applying attention regularization techniques (EAR and KLAR), the model was able to focus on a broader contextual set of words, enabling it to generate much more specific, diverse, and cogent counter narratives defending targeted religious groups. Regularized models performed exceptionally well at generalizing their counter narrative generation even when a specific religious target was entirely excluded from the training data.
